ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "your_email@example.com"

Press Enter through the prompts to use the default:

~/.ssh/id_ed25519

Then display your public key:

cat ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub

If your 42 environment specifically requires an RSA key like the one you showed:

ssh-keygen -t rsa -b 4096 -C "your_email@example.com"

Then:

cat ~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub
Check which keys you already have
ls -la ~/.ssh

Look for:

id_ed25519
id_ed25519.pub

or:

id_rsa
id_rsa.pub

Only copy/share the .pub file. Never share id_rsa or id_ed25519 (without .pub).
